result.title: Counting the Bandages: On measuring the time that AI saves
result.comment: 18 pages, 2 figures. Replaces the author's earlier TSB proposal (SSRN 6682338). Code and data: https://github.com/solomonshalom/tsb-bench. Also archived on Zenodo: 10.5281/zenodo.23557773
result.summary: I consider what it means for AI assistance to save time. I contrast a stopwatch view, on which time saved is whatever the clock records, with a ledger view, on which it is a counterfactual that has to be read next to the errors the work lets through, and I argue for the latter. The argument has four parts. I define a model-free pair of quantities, time saved and excess escaped defects, and one decision number built from them: the break-even defect cost. I give a baseline model of checking in which, until the model is good enough not to check, a calibrated worker's escaped-defect rate does not depend on how good the model is; checking time grows with the logarithm of the model's error rate; and over-trust buys minutes on the clock at a larger cost in total minutes. I show what randomized studies can and cannot identify, and I replicate METR's developer study from its public data: the same 246 issues support a slowdown of 19% or 24% depending on the estimand (34% without adjusting for a chance imbalance), and AI helped on somewhere between 3% and 82% of them. Finally, I restate the published record, with stated bounds in place of imported point assumptions. In GDPval's own review-every-output workflow, review time alone caps GPT-5's speedup at 3.6x; the consultants outside the frontier were faster, and more often wrong. Last, I test two of the model's predictions in a small pre-specified experiment on AI reviewers checking AI drafts of the same kind of brief, built from SEC filings made after the models' training data were collected. Told the drafter's true error rate, the reviewer checked more as it rose, but all-or-nothing, switching near where its prompt's costs break even. Told that the drafter erred ten times less often than it did, it checked 7 fewer of 9 figures and let a wrong figure through in 22.5% of briefs instead of none: faster and worse, entirely through reduced effort.

AI.brief_summary: 主张用「时间节省＋逃逸缺陷」的账本式度量取代单纯计时，提出盈亏平衡缺陷成本作为决策数，建立检查行为基线模型，并复现 METR 开发者研究、用小规模预注册实验检验其预测。
AI.relevance_reason: 把「是否继续核查」写成检查成本与漏检代价的权衡，可为 LVR 中 STOP 决策与视觉证据核验的收益—成本度量、过度信任分析提供概念参照，但未涉及 latent 状态或多模态推理本身，可供核查迁移可能。
